seo.description: Loft conversions in Gravesend, including the L-shaped dormers that suit the town's Victorian terraces, giving a big bedroom and a bathroom in the return. Free site visit

image.alt: Loft conversion on a family home in Gravesend by J Berry Construction

paragraphs: Gravesend is a town of Victorian and Edwardian terraces, and those houses convert beautifully once you understand how they are built. Most have a two-storey "back addition", the rear projection that originally held the kitchen and scullery, and the classic conversion here is an L-shaped dormer that wraps around both the main roof and that back addition, giving a large bedroom over the house and, very often, a bathroom tucked into the return. It is one of the most rewarding conversions there is, and one of the most particular to get right on a terrace. We convert lofts across Gravesend and the surrounding area, on terraces, semis and modern homes alike. Call 07920 731533 or request a callback.

homes.title: Party walls and building in a terrace
homes.intro: Building a loft on a terrace brings two realities that a detached house does not, and being straight about both is part of doing the job properly.
homes.body: The first is party walls. In a mid-terrace house you share a wall with a neighbour on each side, and because a loft conversion involves work to or near those walls, inserting steel, building the new floor, the Party Wall Act usually applies to both. That means serving the correct notices on both neighbours and agreeing the arrangements before work starts. It is a standard process, not a hurdle, and we handle the notices and timing for you so it is done correctly and without souring relations next door.
homes.closing: The second is access. Terraces rarely have side access, so scaffolding goes up at the rear, and materials in and rubble out have to come through the house or via whatever rear route exists, sometimes an alley, sometimes by agreement with a neighbour. It calls for care, protection of your home as we work, and a tidy, considerate site, which on a terrace matters as much to you as to the people either side. The staircase, meanwhile, is usually taken up over your existing stairs, so it uses circulation space rather than costing you a bedroom below. None of this is a problem on a well-run job; it is simply the reality of a terrace, and knowing it upfront is part of what you are paying an experienced builder for.

extensionTypes.title: What suits your Gravesend roof
extensionTypes.intro: The conversion follows your roof. A Victorian or Edwardian terrace with a back addition suits the L-shaped dormer described above; a terrace without a back addition suits a straightforward rear dormer; an end-of-terrace or semi with a hipped roof may suit a hip-to-gable; a house with good head height may need only a rooflight conversion; and the town's modern homes convert in the standard ways, some with trussed roofs needing extra steel and reworking. We match the conversion to your actual roof and, on a terrace, to how it sits with the houses either side.

faqs.q: What is an L-shaped dormer, and why does it suit my Victorian terrace?
faqs.a: It is a dormer built in two joined arms that follow the shape of a typical Victorian terrace: one across the rear of the main roof, the other along the top of the two-storey back addition, meeting at the valley where the two roofs join. It suits these houses because it uses the whole rear roofspace, giving a large full-height bedroom over the main house and, very often, a bathroom in the return over the back addition, so you gain a proper suite. It is the classic conversion for terraces like Gravesend's.

faqs.q: Do I need party wall agreements with both neighbours in a mid-terrace?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. In a mid-terrace house you share a wall with a neighbour on each side, and because the conversion involves work to or near those walls, the Party Wall Act generally applies to both. That means serving the correct notices on both neighbours and agreeing arrangements before work begins. It is a standard, manageable process, and we handle the notices and timing for you so it is done properly.

faqs.q: How do you access a terraced house with no side entrance for a loft conversion?
faqs.a: Scaffolding goes up at the rear, and materials in and rubble out come through the house or via whatever rear route exists, an alley, or by agreement with a neighbour, with your home protected as we work. It calls for a careful, tidy, considerate approach, which on a terrace matters as much to you as to the neighbours either side. It is entirely routine on a well-run job; it simply needs an experienced team that respects the house and the street.

faqs.q: Can I get a bathroom in my loft conversion?
faqs.a: Very often, yes, and on a Victorian terrace the back addition makes it natural. An L-shaped dormer lets the return over the back addition become a bathroom or ensuite, while the main part becomes the bedroom, so you gain a full suite. Even without a back addition, a bathroom can usually be planned into a dormer conversion where there is room. We design the layout so the plumbing and space work sensibly.

faqs.q: What type of loft conversion suits my Gravesend house?
faqs.a: It depends on the roof. A Victorian or Edwardian terrace with a back addition suits an L-shaped dormer; a terrace without one suits a rear dormer; an end-of-terrace or hipped semi may suit a hip-to-gable; a house with good head height may need only a rooflight conversion; and modern homes convert in the standard ways. We match the type to your roof at the site visit.

faqs.q: Do I need planning permission for a loft conversion in Gravesend?
faqs.a: Often not. Many rear dormers, L-shaped dormers and rooflight conversions are permitted development within the volume limits and the front-dormer rule. Mansards, front dormers and conversions in the riverside conservation areas usually need permission. Every conversion needs full building-regulations approval regardless, and the Party Wall Act usually applies on a terrace. We check your position and handle whichever route applies.

faqs.q: Do you also do extensions in Gravesend?
faqs.a: Yes. If a loft cannot give you enough space, or you need ground-floor room too, we design and build extensions in Gravesend, see our Gravesend extension page. On a terrace, a loft conversion and a rear or side-return extension can work well together, and we will advise honestly on the best combination.
